title: How the Mosconi Cup Works: Format, Teams and How to Watch in 2026
description: New to the Mosconi Cup? Learn how Team USA vs Team Europe works, how players qualify, how the scoring gets to 11 points, and how to watch in Orlando Nov 27-30.
body:
Two teams. Five players each. One golden trophy and a roaring crowd. The Mosconi Cup is pool's version of a Ryder Cup showdown, and it returns to Orlando later this month. If you have never watched it, or you tune in once a year and still wonder how the scoring works, this quick guide is for you.

When and where is the 2026 Mosconi Cup?

The 2026 event runs November 27-30 at the Caribe Royale Resort in Orlando, Florida. It is a cheerful, loud, team-style event, which is a big part of why fans love it. You can find it alongside other major events on our big tournaments page and on the pool calendar.

Who plays? Team USA vs Team Europe

The Mosconi Cup is not a single-player tournament. It is a team contest: Team USA against Team Europe, with five players on each side. Johan Ruijsink has been confirmed as the non-playing captain of Team USA. At the time of writing, the Team Europe captain has not yet been announced, so keep an eye out for news.

Europe arrives as the defending champion. Europe won the 2025 edition, played at Alexandra Palace in London, and the official event page calls it Europe's seventeenth Mosconi Cup triumph.

How do players make the team?

Rosters are built from a one-year ranking list. The ranking counts events played after the 2025 Philippines Open. For each team, the top three ranked players qualify automatically. Then two wildcard picks complete the five-player squad, and those players must also meet the event's qualification criteria. The official cut-offs and final line-ups are still to be confirmed, so check back as the event gets closer.

How does the scoring work?

This is the part that surprises new viewers. You are not following one player's bracket. Instead, every match is worth a single point for the team.

  • Each match is a race to five racks. Win five racks first and your team earns one point.
  • Three kinds of matches appear: singles, doubles and team matches.
  • First team to 11 points wins the Cup.

Because every match counts the same, a quick singles win matters just as much as a dramatic team-match finish. A team that falls behind early can come roaring back, and that is what makes the final day so exciting.

What game do they play?

The Mosconi Cup is a nine-ball event, the same fast, run-the-table game that dominates televised pool. New to it? Our 9-ball rules explainer covers how a rack works and what makes a win, and our 8-ball vs 9-ball vs 10-ball guide shows how the games differ.

Who was Willie Mosconi?

The Cup is named after Willie Mosconi, one of the most famous champions in pool history. He is remembered for his skill, his showmanship and a legendary 526-ball run in 1954. You can read the full story in our 526-ball run guide. Putting his name on a team trophy is a nice nod to the sport's past while the biggest stars of today battle for it.

What to watch for as a new fan

Team events have their own rhythm, so here are a few things that make viewing easier and more fun.

  • The break. Every rack starts with a powerful break. A good one can pocket a ball and leave a clear path, and a bad one can hand the table to the opponent.
  • Safety play. When no good shot is available, players hide the cue ball behind other balls so the opponent has a tough time. It looks quiet, but it is real chess on felt.
  • Doubles teamwork. In doubles, partners work together on strategy. Watch for the quick huddles and encouraging taps on the shoulder.
  • The crowd. Team events often bring cheering, chanting and flags. It feels more like a ball game than a quiet tournament, which is great for first-time viewers.

A quick glossary

  • Rack: one game, from the break until the 9 ball falls.
  • Race to five: the first player or side to win five racks takes the match.
  • Wildcard: a captain's pick or special selection to complete the five-player squad.
  • Non-playing captain: the leader who guides the team from the sideline instead of playing.

How to watch

An announced agreement puts the Mosconi Cup and the US Open Pool Championship on ESPN in the United States. The official event page also points fans to WNT TV (wnttv.com). Broadcast details can change, so confirm times and channels on the official World Nineball Tour pages before the first session.

Fun ways to follow along

  • Pick a side with friends. Team USA or Team Europe? A friendly rivalry makes every rack more fun.
  • Keep a simple scoreboard. Count team points up to 11 as the matches finish.
  • Plan a watch party. Check our this weekend page for local pool events and tournaments.

The bottom line

Think of the Mosconi Cup as pool with a team jersey on: five players per side, three match types, races to five, and the first team to 11 points lifts the trophy. Once you know that, the whole weekend clicks. Will Europe defend its title in Orlando, or can Team USA take it back?
